conviction_note: Near-honest zero. JAFCO publishes no earnings forecast. Its dividend is fixed by the DOE-6% floor (interim 66.50 already set), and buybacks are tied to the fiscal-year-end net-cash test, so items 1-3 of the bar are structurally absent at this H1 print. What is left is the H1 capital-gain number. The public exit flow (one locked-up IPO, small JSH and Izawa sell-downs in the 5% filings, no Q2 M&A exit notice) points to a weak quarter, but anyone could see that from the same filings. The one positive is the post-IPO doubling of Tier IV, and it is unrealised or unconfirmed. The two findings offset (sum 0.0). p_up of 48 on a 2.3% scale gives -0.09.
bar: IFIS consensus FY3/2027 ordinary profit 7,800m yen (net 6,200m), unchanged for four weeks, probably one analyst: https://kabuyoho.jp/reportAnalyst?bcode=8595 . The company gives no forecast (Q1 短信: 業績予想は行わず). The H1 bar is that figure pro-rated, about 3.9bn yen. Only one estimate source exists, so the bar is weak and every finding is capped small.

findings.finding: The disclosed Q2 (Jul-Sep 2026) exit flow is thin. The only investee IPO was Tier IV on 7/22, where JAFCO SV5 held 6.9% pre-IPO under a 180-day lock-up. JAFCO's own 5% filings show small listed sell-downs: JSH from 21.56% to 2.51% (about 1.08m shares at roughly 540 yen, about 0.58bn yen at fund level), Izawa Towel from 9.48% to 7.62% (about 0.15bn), and C Channel exited at 30 yen. There was no M&A exit notice in Q2, against Q1's C&J HD sale. On top of Q1 net income of 564m (Q1 capital gain 1,221m), H1 likely lands well below the 3.9bn pro-rata IFIS bar.

findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The exit notices are on TDnet and the sell-downs are in public 5% filings, so a weak H1 is inferable by anyone, and the stock has drifted from 2,355 (early July) to 2,226 with no bounce. What would make it not fully priced: the 5.69 margin ratio, which is a leveraged long that has to sell a confirmed miss, and the static 7.8bn IFIS number, which nobody has marked down. If it were fully priced, IFIS would have been cut or the margin long would have unwound. Neither has happened. The holders own it for the DOE-floored 133-yen dividend, which a weak H1 cannot touch.
findings.independence: Q1 短信 (a different document) shows Q1 capital gain at 51.6% of last year's pace and investment-loss provisions up (coverage 19.3% to 20.5%), the same direction: https://f.irbank.net/pdf/20260724/140120260723598535.pdf . The JAFCO TDnet list shows only one Q2 exit announcement (Tier IV), against two in Q1: https://irbank.net/8595/ir

findings.finding: Tier IV (593A), where JAFCO SV5 held 6.9% pre-IPO, listed on 7/22 at an opening price of 1,009 (below the 1,085 offer) and traded at 2,281 by 10/28, peaking near 2,870 at end-August. That lifts JAFCO's listed portfolio and BPS (PBR 0.87). If a typical 1.5x-offer lock-up release applied, it may also have allowed a realised gain in Q2.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean precedent. The Q1 FY3/27 balance sheet already showed listed holdings at 21.9bn yen book against a 1.2bn yen cost with no visible reaction benefit (Q1 reaction -2.0%). Unrealised gains go to equity, not to profit or the DOE dividend base (株主資本).
findings.source_date: 2026-07-22 (JAFCO notice of Tier IV listing); holder table https://kabu.bridge-salon.jp/ipo-202607-593a/ ; prices https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/593A.T
findings.why_not_priced: The Tier IV move is public but is not reflected in JAFCO's last reported BPS (2,544 at 6/30). The stock has not moved with Tier IV's doubling (JAFCO went from 2,242 to 2,226 while Tier IV roughly doubled), so the market is either ignoring it or assuming the fund cannot sell. Whether any realised gain exists could not be confirmed: the post-IPO stake is about 4%, below the 5% reporting line, and the Tier IV registration statement and lock-up terms were not text-readable here.
findings.independence: none (the fund's stake comes from one IPO-summary page and prices from Yahoo; no second source shows a sale)

outside_window.finding: The shareholder-return policy ties buybacks to the fiscal-year-end 'net usable cash' test (FY3/25 precedent: up to 5bn yen announced with full-year results on 2025-04-23; none at the Oct-2025 H1, only a cancellation). The next natural buyback decision is the FY3/27 results in late April 2027.

baseline_tension: Agrees mildly with the margin-overhang lean (-0.39) and the flat run-up, and adds almost nothing to them. The strongest positive the release could carry is a buyback (looked for: policy ties it to FY-end, so unlikely) or a realised Tier IV gain (looked for, could not confirm). The strongest negative is a visible, already-public thin exit quarter, so the net is about zero.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on public data): the thin-exit finding rests on public TDnet notices and 5% filings, so it went from -0.5 to -0.3 and p_up from 46 to 48
